summary:
SANSIGHT is an AI-powered health monitoring prototype designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions, with a focus on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS).

Unlike systems that analyze individual eye scans, SANSIGHT combines OCT image classification with longitudinal monitoring to track changes in each eye over time. It uses Kalman filtering to estimate measurement trends and uncertainty, data integrity checks to identify missing or low-quality measurements, and adaptive scheduling to prioritize future eye examinations based on changing conditions and limited crew time.

We trained a ResNet-18 model for four-class OCT image classification, achieving 96.5% test accuracy on 1,000 images. Our development also involved two OCT datasets containing more than 110,000 images.

The prototype brings together eye monitoring, vital signs, daily health check-ins, and dashboards for astronauts and Mission Control.

SANSIGHT aims to move beyond isolated health measurements toward more reliable, continuous monitoring and smarter follow-up decisions, supporting greater astronaut autonomy on future lunar and Mars missions.
details:
SANSIGHT — Project Details

Project Overview

SANSIGHT is an AI-powered astronaut health monitoring prototype developed to support health assessment and decision-making during long-duration space missions. Our project focuses on Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), a condition associated with structural changes in the eyes during spaceflight.

The main challenge we address is that analyzing a single eye scan is not enough to understand how an astronaut’s eye health changes over time. Additionally, limited crew time, missing measurements, and variable scan quality make continuous health monitoring more challenging.

SANSIGHT addresses these limitations by combining AI-based OCT image analysis, longitudinal eye monitoring, data integrity checks, adaptive scan scheduling, and vital signs monitoring within one platform.

How SANSIGHT Works

1. AI-Powered OCT Image Analysis

We developed image classification models using ResNet-18 and transfer learning.

Our four-class OCT classification model was evaluated on 1,000 test images and achieved 96.50% test accuracy and 96.49% macro F1-score.

We also developed a separate model for classifying normal, papilledema, and pseudopapilledema images.

2. Longitudinal Eye Monitoring

Rather than evaluating each scan independently, SANSIGHT tracks retinal measurements over time, separately for the left and right eyes.

We implemented Kalman filtering to estimate measurement trends and uncertainty, supporting monitoring when observations are noisy or incomplete.

3. Data Integrity Monitoring

Our system identifies missing, delayed, and low-quality measurements. This helps distinguish reliable observations from data that may require additional attention.

4. Adaptive Scan Scheduling

One of SANSIGHT’s main innovations is its adaptive scheduling approach.

Instead of relying exclusively on fixed examination intervals, the system prioritizes future scans based on changes from baseline, measurement uncertainty, data quality, time since the last valid scan, and available crew time.

For example, if one eye shows greater changes than the other, the system can recommend prioritizing that eye when examination time is limited.

5. Astronaut Health Dashboard

The prototype includes health monitoring features such as vital signs, daily health check-ins, eye measurements, and health trends.

A separate Mission Control dashboard provides an overview of crew health information, monitoring trends, alerts, and scan priorities.

Data and Technical Development

We worked with two OCT image datasets containing a combined 110,438 images.

The first dataset contained 109,309 images across four categories: CNV, DME, DRUSEN, and NORMAL. The second contained 1,129 images for a separate optic-disc-related classification task.

We performed data quality inspection, identified exact duplicate images, and prepared datasets for model training and evaluation.

Our development tools and technologies include:

  • Python: AI model training, data processing, and monitoring algorithms.
  • PyTorch: Deep learning and ResNet-18 transfer learning.
  • Kalman Filtering: Longitudinal measurement estimation and uncertainty tracking.
  • Adaptive Scheduling Algorithms: Prioritizing follow-up examinations under crew-time constraints.
  • FastAPI: Backend services.
  • React and TypeScript: Interactive web dashboards.
  • GitHub: Source code management and team collaboration.

The current prototype uses existing OCT image datasets and simulated longitudinal scenarios to demonstrate the monitoring and scheduling workflow.

Innovation and Creativity

SANSIGHT’s innovation is not limited to applying AI to medical images.

Our approach connects four important capabilities: understanding scan content, monitoring changes over time, checking measurement reliability, and recommending the next examination.

We also track each eye independently, allowing the scheduling logic to consider differences between the left and right eyes.

By incorporating measurement uncertainty and limited crew time, SANSIGHT explores a more practical approach to astronaut health monitoring than isolated scan analysis alone.

Benefits and Intended Impact

SANSIGHT aims to support greater astronaut autonomy, more informed health monitoring, and better prioritization of medical examinations during long-duration missions.

Its potential benefits include earlier recognition of concerning measurement trends, improved awareness of data quality, and more efficient allocation of limited examination time.

These capabilities could be valuable for future lunar and Mars missions, where communication delays, limited medical resources, and increasing distance from Earth make autonomous health monitoring especially important.

Project Scope and Future Development

SANSIGHT is currently a research prototype rather than a clinically validated medical device.

Future development includes evaluating the complete monitoring and scheduling system against longitudinal astronaut health data, conducting quantitative comparisons with fixed scheduling approaches, and validating its performance in realistic operational conditions.

Our long-term vision is to move astronaut health monitoring beyond individual measurements toward a system that understands changes over time and supports smarter follow-up decisions.

SANSIGHT — Beyond the Visible.
